statement: Syntactic or classificatory diversity is not equivalent to inferential diversity. A corpus may draw on multiple independent external sources, vary lexically, and span several classification labels while still possessing very little reasoning-bearing structure — so a measure of source count, lexical distance, or type-label spread is not evidence that the corpus can support inference, and must never be substituted for one.
classification: AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM ABOUT CORPORA, not a definition, method or governance rule — which is why it stays a candidate. Per this repo's Hypothesis-vs-Canon discipline, a claim about the world that experiments exist to test may not enter the canon as ratified before its evidence exists; doing so would undermine the falsifiability the research programme depends on. Crystal vP1 is ONE observation consistent with it (multiple external sources, lexical variation and classificatory spread, alongside near-zero inferential capacity as measured by conjunction entailment). One observation of a distinction is not the distinction established.

canaries.assertion: On a 15-statement fixture of bare necessity generalities, the LABEL-DIVERSITY proxy reads 1.0 (every member carries semanticType constraint|law, clearing the retired 20% bar) while `assessInferentialCapacity` reports 0 relational members, 0 entailment chains and an inferential-capacity fraction of 0, and `derivation-headroom` fails. The two measures are asserted in the same test so that any change collapsing them back into one fails the build.

occurrences.defect: The gate read `semanticType ∈ {constraint, law}` OR a logical-connective word and reported the result as evidence that the collection was 'not only atomic assertions'. A corpus of bare 'X is essential for Y' generalities scored 100% on that proxy and passed, while its conjunctions entailed nothing unstated — so the 12 registered derivation tasks and the generative-sufficiency probe had nothing to measure.

Operator, verbatim (2026-08-26): 'I would leave "Syntactic or classificatory diversity is not equivalent to inferential diversity" at candidate/validated status until we have at least vP1 and vP2 evidence showing the distinction survives a materially improved substrate. That would turn it from a good retrospective observation into something much more defensible.' So: vP1 evidence ALONE is not sufficient, and passing vP2 readiness is not sufficient either. What is required is a measurement on a MATERIALLY IMPROVED substrate (vP2) in which the two measures still come apart — i.e. the distinction is shown to be a real property of corpora rather than an artifact of a weak one.

A `ratified` or `canonical` status additionally requires a named operator act in `ratifiedSource`, which no agent may supply. `validated` additionally requires two recorded occurrences or demonstrated regression prevention; only one occurrence exists.

This is the retrospective observation the remediation cycle preserved, and it is deliberately the WEAKEST-status output of that cycle. The three sibling candidates from the same resolution are engineering rules about how gates must be built; this one is a claim about the world, and it carries a higher evidence bar for exactly that reason.
